u2fd: Show notification only when cr50 requests presence Currently we pre-emptively show the 'touch power button' notification when we receive a request that we know will require user presence. This change instead waits for cr50 to reject the request based on absence of user presence before showing the notification. This change is mainly motivated by the fact that on a system with multiple U2F devices, Chrome will iterate through all and attempt to authenticate against them; we should not request presence pre-emptively in this case as the key handle may belong to another device. BUG=chromium:982790 TEST=[using g2ftool] check notification always displayed for register check notification not displayed for non-owned KH check notification not displayed if presence already known Change-Id: I4a65c4adc3792236314c51340b9d71f2aec2d611 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1736328 Tested-by: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

u2fd: Always ignore Chrome's bogus register messages Chrome may send a 'bogus' REGISTER message, with a fixed/known App ID and Challenge. These are used to cause a USB key to flash it's LED. These change was made in response to user feedback, specifically related to USB keys. It does not make sense to display the 'touch power button' notification (which is intended to replace the LED) in this case, since the user feedback being addressed was around being unsure whether the device was correctly plugged in. So, we simply ignore these messages altogether. BUG=chromium:982790 TEST=[using demo.yubico.com and Google.com] check notification always displayed for register check notification not displayed for non-owned KH Change-Id: Idad446aa3452d54e6c73a28af936b04f14cdf67b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1736329 Tested-by: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Louis Collard <louiscollard@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Adam Langley <agl@chromium.org>

shill: point ethernet_any to first available Ethernet service There are a set of assumptions that Chrome makes when applying service policies that aren't currently upheld with regards to the ethernet_any service (i.e. ethernet_any is not in the ServiceCompleteList, and the service path returned when ethernet_any is configured is not the same one returned after a device is plugged in). We address that in this change by pointing ethernet_any to the first available Ethernet service (dictated by the service sorting heuristic). The algorithm is as follows: when a new Ethernet service is created first check to see if there are currently any Ethernet services. If there aren't, simply assign the new Ethernet device to the existing ethernet_any service instead of instantiating a new one. This way, the service path remains the same if ConfigureServiceForProfile was called before a device was plugged in. If this device is removed at some point, point ethernet_any at the first Ethernet service in the list. This service will now act as the ethernet_any service. If, at some point, the last Ethernet device is unplugged, instead of destroying the service, convert it back to the generic ethernet_any service by removing the associated device and setting the storage identifier to "ethernet_any". TODO: if there are multiple Ethernet services and the default service changes, the GUID remains the same. Chrome may expect the GUID and service path to be consistent, so this will probably need to be corrected. dev-libs/glib: Fix units for 'gdbus wait --timeout' This is to fix an upstream glib bug https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/issues/1737. Without this, 'gdbus wait --timeout N <service-name>' command only waits for the service for N milliseconds while the commands document clearly says says that the unit of the --timeout option is in seconds. All of CrOS usage of gdbus wait are 'gdbus wait --timeout 15 <service-name>', and waiting for the service only for 15ms is most likely way too short, which may cause unexpected races or failures. This CL will fix such potential issues as well as b/139313156 which is known. The patch file was taken from https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/commit/cf54fc36003ed50055b094a2d389a12621fe2700.diff without any modifications. BUG=b:139313156 TEST=emerge-$BOARD glib, cros deploy, run 'time gdbus wait --timeout 3 --system foo.bar', verify the command returns after waiting for the service for about 3 seconds.
